Un margen bruto que baja mientras las ve: A gross margin that falls while sales rise usually means price is being given away or direct costs got out of hand.
El EBITDA no es caja: no descuenta inver: EBITDA is not cash: it does not deduct investments, working capital, interest or taxes.
Si el margen operacional es bajo y el ne: If the operating margin is low and the net margin is high, profit probably comes from non-operating income that will not repeat.
Compara siempre el margen neto con el op: Always compare net margin with operating margin: the gap is what interest, taxes and other items consume.
Una empresa puede mostrar utilidades y a: A company can show profits and still have negative free cash flow if it invests heavily or finances its customers.
Si el EBITDA es positivo pero la convers: If EBITDA is positive but conversion is low, the problem is not margin but working capital or investments.
Un ROA bajo en una empresa con muchos ac: A low ROA in an asset-heavy company is normal: compare it with companies in the same sector.
Un ROE alto con endeudamiento muy alto n: A high ROE with very high debt is not strength: it is risk.
Cada día que se acorta el cobro libera c: Every day the collection period shrinks frees up cash without selling another peso.
Inventario que no rota es caja detenida: Inventory that does not turn is idle cash and an obsolescence risk.
Los proveedores son financiación gratuit: Suppliers are free financing only as long as agreed terms are respected.
Un ciclo largo exige capital de trabajo:: A long cycle demands working capital: without cash, it is paid with debt.
Los negocios de margen bajo necesitan ro: Low-margin businesses need to turn over a lot; high-margin ones can turn over less.
Una rotación que cae suele avisar antes: A falling turnover often warns before sales do that something is not selling.
Si los gastos crecen más rápido que las: If expenses grow faster than sales, the margin is eating itself.
Crecer consume capital de trabajo: cuant: Growing consumes working capital: the higher this indicator, the more cash each new peso of sales asks for.
Por debajo de 1,0 la empresa debe más a: Below 1.0 the company owes more in the short term than it holds in the short term.
Si la razón corriente es buena pero la p: If the current ratio is good but the quick ratio is weak, liquidity depends on selling inventory.
Una razón de efectivo muy baja deja a la: A very low cash ratio leaves the company one bad month away from a cash crisis.
Un capital de trabajo negativo no siempr: Negative working capital is not always bad (some businesses collect before they pay), but it needs watching.
Cuanto más alto el endeudamiento, menos: The higher the debt ratio, the less room for error the company has in a bad streak.
Con deuda neta positiva y EBITDA negativ: With positive net debt and negative EBITDA there is no way to repay from operations: it is an alert, not a number.
Cuando la cobertura se acerca a 1,0, cas: When coverage nears 1.0, almost all operating profit goes to interest.
Si el costo de la deuda supera el retorn: If the cost of debt exceeds the return on what it finances, borrowing destroys value.
El apalancamiento multiplica las gananci: Leverage multiplies gains in good times and losses in bad times.
Crecer sin sostener el margen y el flujo: Growing without sustaining margin and cash flow is not growing well.
Si el EBITDA crece más rápido que los in: If EBITDA grows faster than revenue, the business is gaining scale.

<b>EBITDA.</b> El modelo no trae una lín: EBITDA. The model has no “EBITDA” line: it is calculated as Operating profit + depreciation and amortization (cost and expense), the same rule as in the Income statement report.
Los indicadores que usan el PYG o el Flu: The indicators that use the P&L or the Cash flow add up the 12 months ending at the cut-off month. This prevents a good or bad month, or seasonality, from distorting the result.
Los indicadores que usan el Balance (liq: The indicators that use the Balance sheet (liquidity, leverage, turnovers) take the balance of that month. Days and turnovers combine the cut-off balance with the flows of 12 months.
El mes de comparación se evalúa <b>igual: The comparison month is evaluated the same as the cut-off, with its own 12 months. Options: previous year-end (December, by default), previous month or same month of the previous year.
La variación se muestra en la unidad nat: The variation is shown in the natural unit: percentage points (pp) for percentages, times for ratios and days for terms. Green = the change favors the business; red = it works against it.
<b>Menos de 12 meses de PYG:</b> los ind: Fewer than 12 months of P&L: the indicators that annualize (days, turnovers, returns and growth) are not calculated and are marked “Requires 12 months of data”. The margins are shown but without a traffic light (gray). Nothing is ever annualized.
<b>Crecimiento:</b> necesita 24 meses de: Growth: needs 24 months of history (12 against the previous 12).
<b>Sin Balance en el mes de corte:</b> n: No Balance sheet in the cut-off month: there is no liquidity, leverage or turnovers; the screen says so.
<b>Casos especiales:</b> deuda neta con: Special cases: net debt with non-positive EBITDA is shown as an explicit red alert (there is no number); interest coverage without financial expenses is marked “No financial expenses”; cash conversion with non-positive EBITDA does not apply.

¿Por qué un indicador sale «Requiere 12: Why does an indicator say “Requires 12 months of data”?
Porque la empresa tiene menos de 12 mese: Because the company has fewer than 12 months of P&L in the window ending at the cut-off. To avoid misleading with annualized figures, those indicators are not calculated until the 12 months are complete.
¿Por qué el margen se ve pero sin color?: Why is the margin visible but without color?
Con menos de 12 meses el margen es válid: With fewer than 12 months the margin is valid but its ranges are designed for a full year, so it is shown in gray.

El flujo libre incluye capital de trabaj: Free cash flow includes working capital and investments: a month with delayed collections or asset sales can leave more cash than EBITDA. Look at the trend, not a single cut-off.

<b>Qué mide.</b> Qué parte de los ingres: What it measures. The share of revenue left after covering the cost of sales (COGS and its depreciation). It shows pricing power and control over direct costs.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Revisar precios y: How to improve it. Review prices and discounts, renegotiate with suppliers, cut waste and sell more of what carries the best margin.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Utilidad operativa más: What it measures. Operating profit plus depreciation and amortization over revenue: an approximation of what the business generates before financing and taxes.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Mejorar el margen: How to improve it. Improve gross margin, control administrative and selling expenses and grow without fixed costs rising at the same pace.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Utilidad operacional so: What it measures. Operating profit over revenue: what the core activity leaves after all operating costs and expenses, including depreciation.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Mejorar el margen: How to improve it. Improve gross margin, remove expenses that do not generate sales and review the productivity of the administrative structure.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Utilidad neta sobre ing: What it measures. Net profit over revenue, after financial expenses, other non-operating income and expenses, and taxes.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Reducir el costo: How to improve it. Reduce financial cost, clean up non-operating expenses and improve operating margins.
Margen de flujo libre operativo <span cl: Operating free cash flow margin Profitability
<b>Qué mide.</b> Flujo de caja libre ope: What it measures. Operating free cash flow (after taxes, working capital and operating investments) over revenue. It comes from the Cash flow model.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Liberar capital d: How to improve it. Release working capital (receivables and inventory), postpone investments that do not add cash and improve operating profitability.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Relación entre el flujo: What it measures. Ratio of operating free cash flow to EBITDA. Close to 100% means almost all EBITDA reaches cash; very low or negative means it stays in receivables, inventory or investments.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Acortar el ciclo: How to improve it. Shorten the collection cycle, lower inventory, negotiate supplier terms and prioritize the highest-return investments.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Utilidad neta de los úl: What it measures. Net profit of the last 12 months over total assets at the cutoff.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Aumentar la utili: How to improve it. Raise profit with the same assets, sell unproductive assets and improve inventory and receivables turnover.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Utilidad neta de 12 mes: What it measures. Net profit over 12 months relative to equity at the cutoff. It is inflated when the company borrows heavily: read it together with leverage.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Mejorar el margen: How to improve it. Improve net margin, turn assets over better and use debt only when the return exceeds its cost.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Días promedio que tarda: What it measures. Average days customers take to pay, estimated from the receivables balance and 12-month sales.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Facturar a tiempo: How to improve it. Invoice on time, set clear terms, follow up on collections and offer early-payment discounts.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Días que, en promedio,: What it measures. Average days inventory stays before it is sold, from the inventory balance and 12-month cost of sales.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Ajustar las compr: How to improve it. Match purchases to demand, clear slow-moving items and plan production better.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Días promedio de pago a: What it measures. Average days to pay current suppliers, from their balance and 12-month cost of sales. More days finance the operation, but paying too late harms the relationship.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Negociar plazos m: How to improve it. Negotiate longer terms without losing discounts or risking supply.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Suma los días de carter: What it measures. Adds receivable days and inventory days and subtracts payable days: the days the company must finance with its own cash.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Acortar el cobro: How to improve it. Shorten collection and inventory and lengthen supplier payment within reason.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Ingresos de 12 meses so: What it measures. 12-month revenue over total assets: how much sales each peso invested in assets generates.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Vender más con la: How to improve it. Sell more with the same structure, dispose of idle assets and avoid investments that do not raise sales.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Costo de ventas de 12 m: What it measures. 12-month cost of sales over inventory at the cutoff: how many times inventory is sold and replenished in the year.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Reducir referenci: How to improve it. Cut slow items, buy in smaller lots and align production with sales.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Peso de los gastos oper: What it measures. Weight of operating expenses (administrative and selling) over 12-month revenue.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Congelar gastos f: How to improve it. Freeze fixed costs, automate processes and grow sales without growing the structure.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Capital de trabajo (act: What it measures. Working capital (current assets minus current liabilities) over 12-month revenue. It shows how much operating investment growth requires. If negative, the short term is not covered and it is flagged red.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Reducir cartera e: How to improve it. Reduce receivables and inventory and negotiate supplier terms.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Activo corriente entre: What it measures. Current assets over current liabilities: how many pesos of short-term assets there are per peso of short-term debt.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Pasar deuda de co: How to improve it. Move debt from short to long term, collect receivables and avoid tying up cash in slow-to-convert assets.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Como la razón corriente: What it measures. Like the current ratio but without inventory, the current asset hardest to turn into cash.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Acelerar el cobro: How to improve it. Speed up collection, reduce inventory and renegotiate near-term maturities.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Caja y bancos entre pas: What it measures. Cash and banks over current liabilities: the strictest liquidity measure.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Mantener un colch: How to improve it. Keep a cash cushion, schedule payments better and negotiate available credit lines.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Diferencia entre el act: What it measures. Difference between current assets and current liabilities. Positive: the short term is covered; negative: there is more short-term debt than short-term assets.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Generar caja oper: How to improve it. Generate operating cash, lengthen debt maturities and reduce unnecessary receivables and inventory.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Pasivo total entre acti: What it measures. Total liabilities over total assets: the percentage of assets financed with debts and obligations.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Capitalizar utili: How to improve it. Capitalize profits, pay down debt with free cash flow and avoid financing assets with short-term debt.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Deuda financiera menos: What it measures. Financial debt minus cash, divided by 12-month EBITDA. It is the measure banks use most to size repayment capacity.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Aumentar el EBITD: How to improve it. Raise EBITDA, use free cash flow to pay down debt and avoid new debt that does not generate a return.
<b>Qué mide.</b> EBITDA de 12 meses entr: What it measures. 12-month EBITDA over financial expenses for the same period.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Refinanciar a men: How to improve it. Refinance at a lower rate, reduce expensive debt and raise EBITDA.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Gastos financieros de 1: What it measures. 12-month financial expenses over financial debt at the cutoff. It is an estimate: financial expenses may include other items and debt changes during the year.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Renegociar tasas,: How to improve it. Renegotiate rates, replace expensive debt with cheaper debt and adjust loan terms.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Activo total entre patr: What it measures. Total assets over equity: how much debt amplifies results, for better and for worse.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Retener utilidade: How to improve it. Retain profits to strengthen equity and moderate the use of debt.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Variación de los ingres: What it measures. Change in revenue over the last 12 months versus the previous 12 months. It needs 24 months of history.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Ampliar clientes: How to improve it. Add customers and channels, adjust prices and protect service to current customers.
<b>Qué mide.</b> Variación del EBITDA de: What it measures. Change in 12-month EBITDA versus the previous 12 months. It needs 24 months of history.
<b>Cómo mejorarlo.</b> Crecer ventas con: How to improve it. Grow sales while controlling expenses and protect margins.
